statement: Use the quotient sphere X = G ∪ B, fixed exterior radius R, and coordinates of Definition 2.3. Let L0 be any countable well-ordered list satisfying compatibility (P), with a countable flag set Σ0. Prescribe also a countable set S0 ⊂ B of mandatory marks containing every singularity of L0. There are a countable well-ordered compatible extension L of L0, with enlarged countable flags, and a countable mark set S ⊃ S0 containing all its singularities, with the following properties. Every normalized diagonal finite-transfer limit of L , retaining the marks S, has a circle-domain image. This conclusion persists after any further countable compatible extension, retaining S and including all additional singularities among the marks. More precisely, let εn > 0 tend to zero and let Hn ⊂ G be increasing compact sets such that every compact subset of G is contained in int Hn for all sufficiently large n. One can choose increasing finite subsets In exhausting the labels of L , finite bordered completions (Qn, gn), nested smooth cores Kn ⊂ G, transferred coordinates ui,n, and normalized conformal maps fn : Q◦ n −→ Ωn, fn(z) = z + O(1/z), where Ωn is a finite circle domain, such that Hn ⊂ int Kn and the following assertions hold. (i) The metric gn is the original spherical metric near Kn. For every i ∈ In, the coordinate ui,n agrees with ui near Kn ∩ Mi, and all its terminal periods are those specified in Theorem 3.1. (ii) The total additional energy satisfies X i∈In ∥dui,n∥2 2,(Qn\Kn)∩Mi,gn < ε2 n. (7.16) For every i ∈ In, if Tn,s ⊂ Mi is a terminal disk and s is nonsingular for ui, its boundary oscillation Ai,n(Tn,s) satisfies      X s: Tn,s⊂Mi s̸=pi [Ai,n(Tn,s) − ai(s)]2 +      1/2 < εn. (7.17) The singularity exclusion is omitted for real coordinates. 58 (iii) Every prescribed mark eventually indexes a terminal disk. All terminal disks have quotient diameter tending uniformly to zero. After passing to a subsequence, fn → f locally uniformly on G, where f is normalized and univalent and f(G) is a circle domain. At each marked end, its distinguished target disks converge to the entire component Kb(f). (iv) All complementary disks of Ωn, and all images of physical points in Q◦ n with |z| ≤ 4R, lie in |w| < 5R. Any prescribed compact source sets, including finitely many smooth contours and their collars at each stage, can be retained in Kn. A retained oriented dust contour has the bounded-side correspondence of Lemma 3.3. For each fixed such contour its bounded target sides lie in a fixed disk, uniformly in n and in the number of retained tests. The finite subsets In carry their inherited order from L ; they need not be initial segments of its well-order. The original coordinates, their masks, and their budgets are unchanged.
